title: January 6 Security, Intelligence & Response Record
methodology: Each J6-S record separates information known at the time, dissemination, operational decisions, assistance requests, authorization, mobilization, deployment, and later oversight findings. Later findings are not presented as contemporaneous knowledge.

records.subject: Federal agencies identified potential threats of violence before January 6
records.summary: Later GAO review found that all ten federal agencies it examined identified potential threats of violence before January 6.
records.limitation: The existence of threat information does not mean every agency possessed the same information or a precise prediction of the attack that occurred.

records.subject: Processing and sharing of threat information
records.summary: Oversight reviews identified shortcomings in how some threat information was processed, disseminated, or incorporated into security planning.
records.limitation: A later oversight finding should be distinguished from what a particular official actually knew at a particular time.

records.subject: Capitol security planning underestimated the potential for an extreme attack
records.summary: Bipartisan Senate review identified intelligence, planning, training, equipment, and command shortcomings affecting Capitol preparedness.
records.limitation: Institutional preparedness findings do not establish individual criminal responsibility.

records.subject: Capitol Police request for immediate National Guard assistance
records.summary: As conditions deteriorated, Capitol Police leadership sought immediate National Guard assistance. The request is one stage in a longer response chain.
records.limitation: The time of a request is not the same as authorization, mission assignment, mobilization, movement, or arrival.

records.subject: National Guard approval and mission-definition process
records.summary: The District of Columbia National Guard operated through a federal command structure, and oversight reviews examined approval procedures and the time required to define and authorize the Capitol mission.
records.limitation: Descriptions of delay should identify which stage of the command and deployment process is being measured.

records.subject: Personnel notification, equipping, briefing, and movement
records.summary: Because Guard personnel were not already staged for a Capitol mission, mobilization required personnel to be notified, equipped, instructed, organized, and moved after authorization.
records.limitation: Mobilization is a separate operational stage from the original request for assistance.

records.subject: Capitol Police, Metropolitan Police, federal agencies, and National Guard response
records.summary: Multiple law-enforcement and military organizations participated in securing the Capitol and surrounding grounds as the emergency developed.
records.limitation: Agency participation should not be treated as proof that all organizations shared a single command structure or identical situational awareness.

records.subject: Bipartisan Senate review of security, planning, intelligence, and response failures
records.summary: The bipartisan Senate review documented breakdowns involving intelligence, Capitol security planning, command procedures, equipment, training, and emergency response.
records.limitation: An oversight report is an institutional finding and should not be presented as a judicial determination of individual guilt.
